ai-at-work.dwp_take: TechCrunch is hosting a founder summit in Boston on November 4 where early-stage and established founders can network with venture capitalists and seasoned entrepreneurs for advice on scaling companies. For digital workplace professionals, this matters because the tools and platforms that shape how we work often emerge from these exact conversations between founders and investors. Honestly, if you're building workplace tech and you're not at events like this, you're probably missing the moment when someone figures out the next thing everyone will pretend they've always needed.

ai-at-work.title: Meta says Muse has over 10M users, with shopping a top activity
ai-at-work.excerpt: Meta Muse users are adopting the app for shopping and personal productivity, the company said during its Q3 earnings call. The AI app now has over 10M users.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Meta's Muse has crossed 10 million users, and people are apparently using it more for shopping than productivity, according to the company's latest earnings call. For digital workplace professionals, this matters because it shows where generative AI adoption is actually happening in real life, outside the enterprise bubble we usually obsess over. The humor here is that Meta built an AI assistant, and users immediately decided the best use case was buying stuff, which tells you everything you need to know about human nature and nothing about enterprise readiness.

ai-at-work.title: While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat
ai-at-work.excerpt: As Amazon blocks AI agents from shopping on its site, Walmart is taking the opposite approach, introducing new technology that lets AI agents make purchases on customers' behalf, with controls over sp
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Amazon is blocking AI agents from using its platform while Walmart is actively enabling them to make purchases on behalf of customers with built-in controls. This matters because it shows two competing visions of how AI integrates into employee workflows and customer experience, which will shape what tools your organization adopts and how you manage automation governance. Walmart's bet is basically "trust but verify" while Amazon's playing it like a nervous parent, and honestly, both approaches will probably end up in your tech stack eventually because your CEO will demand it.

ai-at-work.title: Blacksmith hits unicorn valuation after Sequoia leads Series C
ai-at-work.excerpt: Blacksmith, a platform that lets companies build and test AI code more effectively, just announced a $66 million Series C round led by Sequoia that values the company at $1 billion.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Blacksmith, an AI code development platform, just hit unicorn status with a $1 billion valuation after Sequoia led its $66 million Series C round. This matters because digital workplace teams are increasingly expected to integrate AI tooling into their development workflows, and well-funded platforms like this one will shape what your engineers actually use daily. Here's the thing though: valuation doesn't equal usefulness, and plenty of billion-dollar developer tools have crashed and burned when they didn't solve real problems faster than the free alternatives.

tools-tech.title: GridCraft is the open-source Excel clone for Linux I’ve been waiting for
tools-tech.excerpt: If spreadsheets are your thing, but Microsoft Office isn’t, you might want to give the open-source clone, GridCraft, a try.
tools-tech.dwp_take: GridCraft launched as an open-source Excel alternative for Linux users who want spreadsheet functionality without Microsoft's licensing costs or ecosystem lock-in. For digital workplace teams supporting diverse operating systems and cost-conscious organizations, this matters because it expands platform flexibility and reduces vendor dependency in productivity stacks. That said, I've seen "Excel killers" come and go for three decades, and adoption usually stalls when someone inevitably asks "but does it do what my macro does" and the answer is silence.

tools-tech.title: Chrome warns you about suspicious websites now – how to turn on Google’s new scam protection
tools-tech.excerpt: Google’s browser will flash two types of warnings based on whether the site is deemed dangerous or just suspicious.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google Chrome now shows two levels of website warnings: one for dangerous sites and another for merely suspicious ones. This matters to digital workplace pros because your users will encounter these alerts constantly, and you need to understand what they mean so you can confidently guide employees through false positives without breeding mistrust in the security system. Honestly, I'm glad Google is splitting the difference here because one-size-fits-all warnings train people to ignore everything, and that's how they end up clicking the sketchy link anyway.

tools-tech.title: ServiceNow and Nvidia launch Arc, a new AI agent for enterprise
tools-tech.excerpt: The two companies are trying to solve the AI agent security conundrum with multiple layers of real-time security checks.
tools-tech.dwp_take: ServiceNow and Nvidia built Arc, an AI agent designed to handle enterprise tasks while running security checks in real time to prevent bad actors from hijacking it. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because we're all racing to deploy AI agents into our workflows, and security theater won't cut it when these systems actually have access to your data and systems. Look, I've seen enough botched implementations to know that "multiple layers of security" sounds great until someone finds the first vulnerability, but at least these two are thinking about the problem instead of just shipping it and hoping for the best.

tools-tech.title: Remediation in the era of AI: Fix what matters first
tools-tech.excerpt: Every IT and security team knows the feeling of opening a vulnerability report and seeing a number that only goes up. Thousands of findings. Hundreds marked critical. A backlog that grows faster than
tools-tech.dwp_take: Computerworld reports that vulnerability backlogs have become unmanageable, with AI-powered scanning tools now generating so many findings that traditional triage methods have completely broken down. This matters because digital workplace teams are drowning in alert noise while actual risks go unaddressed, which means your infrastructure security is only as good as your ability to separate signal from noise. My take: We've spent thirty years building better tools to find problems, and now we need to finally admit that working harder isn't a strategy, it's just expensive exhaustion.

digital-culture.title: Half of this group of workers lies to take PTO
digital-culture.excerpt: For pet owners with jobs, occasionally missing work to care for their animals is a matter of routine. So is lying about it. In a recent survey, nearly half (46%) of working pet owners said they usuall
digital-culture.dwp_take: Nearly half of working pet owners admit to lying to their employers about why they're taking time off, with a quarter claiming to have called in sick specifically for pet-related emergencies. This matters because it reveals a massive trust gap between employees and managers, suggesting that workplace policies around PTO and flexibility are so rigid that people feel forced to fabricate excuses rather than be honest. After three decades watching workplace culture, I can tell you that any environment where nearly 50% of your workforce feels they need to lie about their time off isn't a flexibility problem, it's a leadership problem.

digital-culture.title: The hidden cost of being the ‘reliable one’ at work
digital-culture.excerpt: Being the always reliable team member at work can earn trust—but it can also limit your growth and cause burnout. Below, experts share how to challenge unfair expectations, set clear boundaries, and a
digital-culture.dwp_take: The article highlights how being the dependable workhorse in your organization can trap you in a role where you're underutilized, underpromoted, and burning out while others advance. This matters because digital workplace professionals often get cast in this role early on, becoming the go-to person for everything from Sharepoint migrations to Slack emergencies, and nobody questions whether you're actually developing new skills. The real kicker is that management secretly loves this arrangement because it lets them avoid harder conversations about workload and succession planning, so you've basically volunteered for career stagnation.

digital-culture.title: Workforce data, smarter AI integration among greatest workplace priorities in the new year
digital-culture.excerpt: The importance of workforce data is just one of the prognostications people managers are making looking to the year ahead.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies are prioritizing workforce data and AI integration as top workplace initiatives for the coming year, according to new research from WorkLife. This matters because digital workplace pros need to understand that data strategy and AI implementation are no longer nice-to-haves but foundational to how organizations will operate, which means you'd better start thinking about governance, privacy, and adoption strategies now. Here's the thing though: most organizations will collect the data and deploy the AI without actually knowing what problem they're solving, which is exactly backwards but somehow totally predictable.

digital-culture.title: Airbnb Hosts Are Furious They Can No Longer Make Guests Do Their Chores
digital-culture.excerpt: Some hosts are threatening to strike, while others are plotting ways around Airbnb’s new restrictions. Guests, meanwhile, are celebrating.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Airbnb quietly removed a feature that let hosts require guests to do chores in exchange for discounts, and now some hosts are threatening to strike over it. This matters because it shows how platform policies around work expectations and fairness directly impact user behavior and satisfaction, something every workplace software maker should watch. The real takeaway: trying to sneak unpaid labor past your users under the guise of "savings" eventually blows up in your face, and rightfully so.

industry-news.excerpt: Critical PHP flaws forced European government websites offline. Learn which PHP versions need patches and what IT teams should do. The post EU Website Outages Follow Critical PHP Flaws: What IT Teams
industry-news.dwp_take: Critical PHP vulnerabilities took down several EU government websites, leaving citizens unable to access essential services. For digital workplace teams, this is a reminder that your infrastructure is only as secure as the code running underneath it, and unpatched systems will eventually bite you. Here's the thing: if government IT shops with actual budgets can't keep PHP updated, what hope do the rest of us have?

industry-news.title: Microsoft Is Removing 8 Copilot Shortcuts From File Explorer — Here’s What Stays
industry-news.excerpt: Microsoft will remove eight OneDrive Copilot shortcuts from File Explorer starting in November 2026, changing how users access AI-powered file tools. The post Microsoft Is Removing 8 Copilot Shortcuts
industry-news.dwp_take: Microsoft is pulling eight OneDrive Copilot shortcuts out of File Explorer come November 2026, forcing users to find new ways to access AI-powered file features they might actually be using. This matters because if your organization built workflows around these shortcuts, you're looking at retraining people and rethinking how they interact with files and AI assistance. Honestly, this feels like Microsoft reorganizing the deck chairs on the Titanic while pretending it's progress, but at least they're giving people a year and a half to adjust.

industry-news.excerpt: Send unlimited files with real-time tracking, custom branding, and GDPR-compliant infrastructure — no fees. The post Transfr Pro Replaces WeTransfer With a Single $79.99 Payment appeared first on Tech
industry-news.dwp_take: Transfr Pro is positioning itself as a WeTransfer alternative that charges a flat $79.99 one-time fee instead of subscription pricing, throwing in unlimited file transfers, tracking, and custom branding. For digital workplace teams that move files constantly, eliminating recurring subscription bloat while getting GDPR compliance built in actually matters when you're managing compliance and budgets. Finally someone's attacking the transfer subscription treadmill, though I'd want to see how their real-time tracking stacks up before ditching WeTransfer's muscle memory.

industry-news.title: Australia Prepares to Sue Meta, TikTok Over Under-16 Social Media Ban
industry-news.excerpt: Australia is preparing legal action against Meta, TikTok, Snap, and Google over alleged breaches of its under-16 social media ban. Here's what could happen next. The post Australia Prepares to Sue Met
industry-news.dwp_take: Australia is suing Meta, TikTok, Snap, and Google for allegedly violating its ban on under-16s using social media platforms. This matters to digital workplace folks because it signals governments are willing to take tech giants to court over compliance, which could reshape how platforms enforce age verification and data policies globally. If Australia wins, expect every workplace intranet and collaboration tool to suddenly require ironclad age verification systems, turning your Slack channels into something resembling airport security.
